reason: The picture shows blood approaching the kidney filter, directly matching the filtering goal.
expectation: The filter should let smaller substances through while keeping blood cells and large proteins in the blood.

alternatives.reason: The ureters also clearly fit the goal of connecting the kidneys to the bladder.

effect: The filter lets useful glucose, salts and water through along with wastes, so the fluid still needs the recovery tube.
reaction: It is interesting that filtering alone does not separate waste from everything useful.
reason: The recovery tube's picture shows useful substances moving back toward the blood.
expectation: Glucose, some salts and much of the water should return toward the blood while waste continues along the tube.

alternatives.reason: I could build the drainage route first instead.

effect: The recovery tube returned useful substances and much water to the blood, leaving waste-containing fluid to collect.
reaction: It makes sense now why filtering and recovery are separate steps.
reason: The kidney pair has a named slot for ureters, which carry fluid toward the bladder.
expectation: The ureters should fit into the kidney pair and provide a route toward the bladder.

alternatives.reason: The bladder is also a named slot, but the ureters connect it to the kidneys.

effect: The ureters now connect to the kidney outlets, leaving the bladder to complete the drainage route.
reaction: The connection follows the pictured route as expected.
reason: The bladder is the remaining named slot and collects fluid from the ureters.
expectation: The bladder should attach to the ureters, completing the route from the kidneys.

effect: The ureters and bladder now form a continuous drainage route; the urinary organs still need connecting to the body.
reaction: The completed route matches the pictures.
reason: The new goal calls for connecting the kidney pair to the body.
expectation: The urinary organs should connect to the body and its blood supply.

alternatives.reason: The remaining fluid also needs to reach the bladder, but the new goal suggests connecting the organs first.

effect: The urinary organs are connected to the body and its circulation; collecting the remaining urine is still the outstanding goal.
reason: The remaining kidney fluid needs to reach the bladder, so I will try it with the connected urinary system.
expectation: The remaining waste-containing fluid should travel through the ureters and collect in the bladder.

effect: The body model was not the accepted partner, but the hint automatically combined the fluid with the fitted kidney pair and completed urine collection.
reaction: I was surprised the separate kidney pair was still the needed partner after connecting it to the body.

mostWorthwhile.text: Filtering and then recovering useful substances was most worthwhile: it showed why the kidneys do more than simply remove waste.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the ureters and bladder was clear but fairly predictable compared with learning what happens to the filtered fluid.

surprise.text: Useful glucose and water passed through the filter along with wastes, so they had to be recovered afterward.

arbitrary.text: Using the separate fitted kidney pair to collect urine felt a little arbitrary after the organs had already been connected to the body, though the compatibility hint resolved it.

continue.text: I would continue into another chapter: following the fluid from filtration through recovery made the organ's job understandable, and I would be curious to see another body system built that way.
